comparison: Both evaluate claims C1-C5 about peripheral blood and bone marrow progenitor changes with age. OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by flow cytometry data, while peer reviewers (Reviewer 3) find the interpretation UNCERTAIN, noting the link between CMP/GMP changes and myeloid-biased HSC expansion is 'misleading' and 'more complex than just a direct correlation.'

Both evaluate claims C6-C9 regarding Hoxb5 as an LT-HSC marker validation. OpenEval finds the validation SUPPORTED by flow cytometry and transplantation data. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN due to fundamental concerns about sample size and representativeness, with Reviewer 1 noting only '3.2 mice experiment for the whole manuscript' and Reviewer 2 citing 'very low number of recipient mice' with 'very large standard deviations.'

Both evaluate claim C10 about similar myeloid proportions across serial transplants. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED but notes it alone is insufficient to rule out myeloid-biased clonal expansion. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED as a descriptive finding, though they note broader methodological concerns about the experiments containing this observation.

Both evaluate claims C11-C13, C70 about similar lineage output between young and aged LT-HSCs. OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (n=8) and large standard deviations. Peer reviewers rate this UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 stating the 'absence of clearly detectable differences...could simply be a false-negative result' and Reviewer 3 noting 'the level of variability...diminishes the robustness of these results.' This is a critical disagreement on a paradigm-challenging claim.

Both evaluate claims C14-C15 about myeloid bias in bulk-HSCs. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED, noting it is consistent with prior literature and serves as an important control showing expected phenotype in mixed HSC populations.

Both evaluate claims C16-C17, C71 about lack of myeloid gene enrichment in aged LT-HSCs. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by RNA-seq and GSEA data. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 identifying a logical inconsistency: if ST-HSCs lack lymphoid enrichment, 'it is hard to understand how aged bulk HSCs have more myeloid gene set enrichment,' suggesting the molecular data do not definitively rule out lineage bias in LT-HSCs.

Both evaluate claims C18-C21 about ST-HSC behavior and memory cell persistence. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED. The data appear internally consistent and this interpretation is not challenged by reviewers.

Both evaluate claim C22 about age-dependent changes in LT-HSC and ST-HSC frequencies. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED as a descriptive observation that forms the basis for the authors' alternative model.

Both evaluate claims about LT-HSC:ST-HSC ratio manipulation experiments. OpenEval (R9: C23-C24, C72) finds this SUPPORTED as a key experiment demonstrating the ratio effect. Peer reviewers (R9: C23-C25, C26, C72) find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 questioning the logic ('not intuitively clear why a reduction of ST-HSCs clones would lead to a myeloid bias') and Reviewer 1 questioning whether the cell numbers represent actual old HSC behavior.

OpenEval R10 evaluates claim C25 (reciprocal experiment with aged cells) and finds it SUPPORTED. This overlaps with peer R9 which includes C25 among claims rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about biological meaningfulness and whether the experiments truly represent old HSC behavior.

Both evaluate the study's main conclusion (C26, C68) that myeloid bias results from altered HSC subset ratios rather than clonal selection. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by convergence of multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, with the editor stating 'current results remain incomplete,' Reviewer 2 concluding the data 'do not convincingly challenge the current paradigm,' and Reviewer 3 noting 'such a strong claim needs to be supported by solid experimental data.'

OpenEval R12 evaluates claims C27, C60 about recipient age effects on myeloid bias and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates overlapping claims C27-C30, C60 about extrinsic niche effects and finds them UNCERTAIN, noting the authors 'did not address the comment regarding inflammatory aged niche effects' and that the irradiation regimen 'might contribute to the uncertainty of the data.'

OpenEval R13 evaluates claims C28-C30 about bone marrow progenitor composition and finds them SUPPORTED despite limited sample size. Peer R10 includes these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, citing unaddressed concerns about inflammatory niche effects and methodological issues with the irradiation regiment.

OpenEval R14 evaluates claims C31-C32 about secondary lymphoid organ dysfunction and finds them SUPPORTED by imaging and flow cytometry. Peer R11 evaluates the same claims (plus C63, C69) and finds them SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 specifically noting 'Their data regarding the role of the microenvironment in the spleen and thymus appears to be convincing.'

OpenEval R15 evaluates claims C63, C69 synthesizing findings about extrinsic contributions and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R11 evaluates these claims (along with C31-C32) and also finds them SUPPORTED, representing one of the few areas of strong agreement between OpenEval and peer reviewers.

Both evaluate claim C59 about the observation that altered LT-HSC:ST-HSC ratios alone cannot fully explain myeloid bias in naturally aged mice. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED as a comparative observation indicating additional factors contribute to the aged phenotype.

OpenEval R17 evaluates claims C35-C67 representing cited background knowledge and prior work, finding them appropriately referenced and SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims specifically.
